Those who have directly hurt you, may not be capable of acknowledging and understanding how you were affected by their actions - even in the worst of cases. Yep... its true. They had no more of a guaranteed parenting success manual than you do at having chances for a perfect marriage. We limp along and do our best. So be sure you have a clear understanding from your wife about what she wants, and work to create an amicable solution. All of this said, seek out supportive friends, and actively work to do your part to make the changes you want to see in your life. One way or the other, you will benefit from it. Be well.

It sounds like you're navigating through a very painful and complex situation with your parental figures, and it's completely understandable to feel lost and unworthy as you process these past experiences. The hurt you've faced can create deep scars that linger, influencing how you see yourself and your worth in other relationships, including with your husband.

It's important to acknowledge that healing from past traumas is not a linear process, and you don't have to rush yourself to "get over" these feelings, especially when you feel invalidated by those around you. It may be helpful to consider speaking with a therapist who can provide a safe space for you to explore your feelings and experiences. Therapy can guide you in understanding your past, defining your identity, and establishing boundaries that protect your emotional well-being.

Additionally, practicing self-compassion can be a valuable tool. Remind yourself that it’s okay to feel hurt and that your emotions are valid. You might also benefit from journaling your thoughts and feelings, which can help you process what you’re experiencing and gain clarity on your identity and desires.

As you navigate this journey, try grounding techniques such as deep breathing or mindfulness exercises to help manage overwhelming emotions. Surrounding yourself with supportive friends or seeking out support groups may also provide comfort and understanding.

Remember, you are worthy of love and respect, and taking steps toward healing is a brave and important journey. You don’t have to do this alone.
